title: Fultium-D3 800 IU Capsules: summary of product characteristics
authors: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency; Thornton & Ross Ltd (marketing authorisation holder)
journal: MHRA Products, marketing authorisation PL 00240/0624; date of revision of the text 1 September 2026
funder: not stated; UK product information carries no funding statement.
result: Indication: treatment and prophylaxis of vitamin D deficiency in adults and adolescents over 12 years with an identified risk; daily dose not to exceed 4000 IU. Contraindications: hypersensitivity, hypervitaminosis D, nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, conditions causing hypercalcaemia or hypercalciuria, severe renal impairment. Patients with pseudohypoparathyroidism, sarcoidosis, or taking thiazide diuretics or cardiac glycosides must be referred to their doctor; during long-term treatment serum calcium and renal function should be monitored, especially in elderly patients taking cardiac glycosides or diuretics and in patients prone to stone formation; the dose should be reduced or stopped if urinary calcium exceeds 300 mg (7.5 mmol) per 24 hours; serum calcium must be monitored at daily doses above 1000 IU. Undesirable effects: hypercalcaemia and hypercalciuria uncommon (more than 1/1000, less than 1/100); hypersensitivity reactions such as angio-oedema or laryngeal oedema, frequency not known. Overdose: hypercalcaemia can severely damage soft tissues and kidneys; symptoms include polyuria, nephrocalcinosis, renal calculi and in severe cases cardiac arrhythmias; extreme hypercalcaemia may result in coma and death; persistently high calcium may lead to irreversible renal damage and soft tissue calcification. Preclinical: high doses were teratogenic in animals; offspring of rabbits given high doses had lesions resembling supravalvular aortic stenosis.
